text: Thank you for sharing that history. To begin our assessment, can you tell me how old your newborn is in days, and when did you first notice the yellowing of the skin and eyes?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-week-old female newborn. The patient has been experiencing increasing yellow discoloration of her eyes and skin for 2 days. She was born at 39 weeks' gestation, initially weighed 3066 g and now weighs 3200 g. The patient is exclusively breastfed.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has your baby passed meconium normally, and are there any other symptoms like poor feeding, vomiting, or fever? REQUEST TEST: Bilirubin_level. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_Ultrasound.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Increasing yellow discoloration of the eyes and skin. I also have Exclusively breastfed, Brother died 3 months after liver surgery.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Born at 39 weeks' gestation. Exclusive breastfeeding. Family history notable for older brother's death possibly related to liver issues. Social history: Not applicable for age.

speaker: Patient
text: Temperature of 37.1°C, pulse of 145/min, and respirations of 40/min. No other symptoms reported by the caregiver. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Acute appendicitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Breastfeeding Jaundice (Physiologic/Pathologic). The clinical picture of a 2-week-old with exclusively breastfed history, increasing jaundice, and normal vital signs is inconsistent with appendicitis; I have ordered a bilirubin level and abdominal ultrasound to confirm and rule out other causes. Please let me know the lab results and ultrasound findings once they are available.
